Operator answers 2026-10-21 (AskUserQuestion) - REQUIREMENTS (RQM-decide), chosen options:
(1) ONE kind `requirement` with class = product|constraint|standard|policy and strengths MUST (block; waive only) / SHOULD (warn; deviate with reason) / MAY (advisory), reusing the goals mapping; no second 'standard' kind.
(2) Layers org > team > project > local > task, a lower layer may only TIGHTEN unless a person records a scoped, reasoned, expiring waiver; agents may propose and accept only the low-risk classes a knob names, a person accepts the rest.
(3) Injection tiers: always-on charter of one line per MUST, capped at 500 tokens (the operator chose the LARGER charter: `[requirements].charter_tokens` default 500, not 250), never trimmed, re-sent after compaction; contextual by glob/context at claim and pre-edit; on-demand search; periodic digest. Remote sources (codeguide, corporate URL) arrive trust=imported, pinned by digest, and are never auto-applied above SHOULD without a person's approval.

Operator answers 2026-10-21 (AskUserQuestion) - SOFT UPGRADES (SU-decision), chosen options:
(1) stable stdlib stdio shim + restartable worker (A+D); in-process reload rejected; hard upgrades use exec-restart.
(2) shim-to-worker transport: stdio pipes to a child process (portable incl. Windows), not a unix socket.
(3) the 5-rung soft/hard rule: soft if the interface digest is unchanged, or the client honours list_changed, or facade mode (ddflow_search/ddflow_call) is on; additive changes soft for every client (new tools appear after restart for clients that ignore list_changed); a changed schema of an existing tool is soft only if the worker accepts the previous arguments for one version; hard = incompatible change to an existing tool/prompt for a client that does not honour list_changed, or the shim/protocol changed; reconnect is a fallback tier only.
(4) learn client capability by client table (clientInfo name) + 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen opt-in + observation (one re-fetch within 10 s = honouring; two silent notifications in different sessions = ignoring), no handshake probe.

Operator answers 2026-10-21 - SEQUENCING: P-soft-upgrade stays right after P-tool-diet (as is); P-requirements stays held behind the core/docs wave per D-old-work-behind-core-docs. Do not change those dependencies.
STALE ITEMS: force-complete the 4 research items RM-client-exec-research, RM-long-ops-research, RM-tool-diet-research, RV-scale-research (docs only, work already merged); LEAVE the 6 fix items and fix...gate-flapping-research open.
DOC PIPELINE: operator confirmed deriving the doc pipeline from declared globs (verified against the actual diff); alternative rejected: explicit kind on MCP task_add (costs tool-schema budget).

data.alternatives: A second 'standard' kind: a second engine and verb set to keep in step. priority as the strength carrier: it orders, it does not oblige.

data.alternatives: Free override by lower layers: an org floor would mean nothing. A [policy] duplicate section: the org floor is B-org-policy.

data.alternatives: 250-token charter: drops MUSTs sooner. Trimming the charter when over budget: a silently missing MUST is worse; over the cap is a doctor finding.
data.decision: Tiers: always-on charter (one line per MUST, [requirements].charter_tokens default 500, never trimmed, re-sent after compaction); contextual by glob/context at claim and pre-edit; on-demand search; periodic digest. Operator chose the larger charter (500, not the recommended 250).

data.alternatives: In-process reload: stale module state, no isolation. Unix socket: not portable to Windows. B or C alone: cannot cover a changed protocol or old clients.
data.decision: Options A+D: stdlib stdio shim owns the client connection, a restartable worker does the work; transport is stdio pipes to a child process (portable incl. Windows); hard upgrades use exec-restart. Operator 2026-10-21.

data.alternatives: Treating every client that ignores list_changed as hard: the facade makes it soft. Reconnect as primary: no client lets a server request one and exit-respawn drops the in-flight call.
data.decision: Soft if the interface digest is unchanged, or the client honours list_changed, or facade mode (ddflow_search/ddflow_call) is on. Additive changes are soft for every client. A changed schema of an existing tool is soft only if the worker accepts the previous arguments for one version. Hard = incompatible change to an existing tool/prompt for a client that does not honour list_changed, or the shim/protocol changed. Reconnect is a fallback tier only.
data.title: Soft upgrades: the 5-rung soft/hard rule; reconnect is a fallback tier only

data.alternatives: A handshake probe: extra round trip and a false signal for clients that answer without acting.
data.decision: Client table by clientInfo name, the 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen opt-in, and observation (one re-fetch within 10 s = honouring; two silent notifications in different sessions = ignoring).
data.title: Soft upgrades: learn client list_changed support by table + listen opt-in + observation, no handshake probe

data.body:
Tier 0 charter: one line per MUST requirement (id, 12 words, strength) capped at [requirements].charter_tokens (default 500, operator D-requirements-injection) in the SessionStart brief and the MCP initialize block, never trimmed (pinned like inject.pinned). Tier 1 contextual: full statement + verify command for requirements matching the item/globs at claim (api/lifecycle/claim.py), in gate prompts (api/gates.py) and in review prompts with the verify-and-cite-id instruction (inject.VERIFY). Tier 2 on demand: `ddflow_recall`/`requirement for` search. Measured on this repo (research doc): SessionStart payload 5,374 B (~1,343 tok), brief 4,208 B, claim guidance block ~304 tok (door budget = 25% of session.brief_max_tokens=1200), agent launch brief 8,787 B (cap 9000), MCP initialize instructions 12,718 chars (~3.2k tok, pointers only, no rule text). The charter must fit inside the existing budget: it REPLACES the unreadable 'N more cut' line, it is not added on top. Acceptance: byte/token caps tested; a MUST requirement is never cut for a SHOULD; dropped ids are listed as '+N more: ddflow requirement for'.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12; shipped defaults overridable per project and org; extend the shared engines instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/requirements-management.md (RQM-research).



COORDINATE: P-change-surface.context-budget measures the always-loaded budget (tool list, instructions, brief) and may trim it; the charter's 500-token cap (default, a knob) is a knob that task must see. SE-hazard-scan / KB-inject fence imported text; requirement text from non-operator sources goes through the same fence (core.provenance).

Extend ddflow/templates/kinds/requirement.toml (today: title, statement, rationale, state, priority, source, stakeholders, tags; lifecycle proposed..verified; inert, ddflow record requirement list works). Add fields: class (product|constraint|standard|policy), strength (must|should|may; keep `priority` as an alias only if D-decide says so), globs[], contexts[] (build-system, language, tool: cmake, conan, cpp ... a context is a named matcher over files, see RQM-scope), gates[], topic (dotted key such as build.system) and expect (the normalised value, e.g. cmake) for conflict detection, verify {kind: command|pattern|file|config|reviewer|mcp, spec, expect_exit, timeout}, source {layer: org|team|project|local|task, uri, rev, digest, fetched_at}, owner, version, supersedes (the record verbs already give supersede/merge/split), review_by. Unknown keys carried, invalid values refused naming the field (core.kinddata). Acceptance: `ddflow record requirement add --set ...` accepts the CMake example of the research doc; validation rejects strength=maybe and a verify without a spec; history/supersede/search work through the record surface; descriptor still loads under B-rc-conformance.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12; shipped defaults overridable per project and org; extend the shared engines instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/requirements-management.md (RQM-research).

DECIDED 2026-10-21 (D-requirements-model, docs/ddflow/decisions/requirements.md): one kind, class product|constraint|standard|policy, strength must|should|may. priority is NOT a strength alias. The charter cap is [requirements].charter_tokens, default 500 (operator chose the larger charter over 250); add the knob here if the model task owns the section.

Ask the operator and file the decision document. Recommended defaults (research section 'Recommended design'): (1) ONE kind `requirement` (the shipped template) with `class` = product|constraint|standard|policy, not a second 'standard' kind; P-product-docs adds EARS/baseline fields to the same descriptor. (2) strength = MUST (block, waive|none) / SHOULD (warn, deviate) / MAY (advisory) reusing the P-goals mapping (D-goals-principles). (3) layers org > team > project > local > task; a lower layer may only TIGHTEN (raise strength, narrow scope, add a verify) unless a person records a scoped, reasoned, expiring waiver. (4) injection tiers: always-on charter capped at [requirements].charter_tokens (default 250), contextual by glob/context at claim and pre-edit, on-demand search, periodic digest at a cadence; compaction re-sends the charter. (5) an agent may PROPOSE a requirement and accept only the low-risk classes the knob names (D-product-docs-r3 pattern); a person accepts the rest. (6) remote sources are trust=imported, pinned by digest, never auto-applied above SHOULD without a person's approval. (7) no `[policy]` duplicate: org enforced floor is B-org-policy. Write docs/ddflow/decisions/requirements.md and record decisions with --globs.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12; shipped defaults overridable per project and org; extend the shared engines instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/requirements-management.md (RQM-research).

DECIDED 2026-10-21: all of (1)-(6) accepted, with ONE change: charter_tokens default is 500, not 250. See docs/ddflow/decisions/requirements.md; decisions D-requirements-model, D-requirements-layers, D-requirements-injection.

Worker = today's Server behind a framed, versioned channel (hello{shim_proto, worker_proto, digest, ddflow version}, request, response, progress/notify passthrough, drain, bye). Stateless per request: connection state (protocol, client_info, agent, called_from) travels with every request as the shim holds it (reuses the DDFLOW_MCP_HANDOFF fields). Reuse the _offload/_worker_main process pattern; rejects an incompatible shim_proto with a typed error so the shim classifies HARD.

DECIDED 2026-10-21 (D-soft-upgrade-architecture, D-soft-upgrade-rule, D-soft-upgrade-capability; docs/ddflow/mcp-soft-upgrade.md): the worker is a child process of the shim over stdio pipes (no unix socket); in-process reload rejected; the worker accepts the previous schema's arguments for one version.

ddflow-mcp entry becomes the shim: under 400 lines, imports only the stdlib (no ddflow.* beyond its own package), starts in about 20 ms, RSS a few MB. Does: line framing, JSON-RPC routing, negotiation, serving the cached interface snapshot, spawning and supervising the worker (crash -> restart and a typed error for the in-flight call, never a dead connection), forwarding with request-id remapping. Must not replay initialize to the worker with a colliding id (prototype flaw). A size/import-purity test enforces the budget. Windows: pipes, no unix socket needed.

DECIDED 2026-10-21 (D-soft-upgrade-architecture, D-soft-upgrade-rule, D-soft-upgrade-capability; docs/ddflow/mcp-soft-upgrade.md): stdlib-only stdio shim; transport to the worker is stdio pipes to a child process (portable incl. Windows), not a unix socket; hard upgrades exec-restart the shim.

No client lets a server request a reconnect (R-soft-reconnect-source-matrix) and exit-and-respawn fails the in-flight call; Claude Code -p respawns lazily but keeps the stale tool list (VERIFIED). So reconnect is rung 4 only: the existing [mcp].on_upgrade=reexec is chosen instead of the restart notice when the table marks the client reconnect=respawn+relist; the report says one in-flight call may fail. Work: (1) run Qwen Code (and VS Code if available) against docs appendix B probe rc.py to learn whether a stdio exit is noticed and tools are re-listed, fill the table; (2) the policy and report text; (3) never reexec when the shim connection is stable. Decide in SU-decision whether to keep it at all: if Qwen does not notice stdio exits the tier has no member and this task is dropped.

DECIDED 2026-10-21 (D-soft-upgrade-architecture, D-soft-upgrade-rule, D-soft-upgrade-capability; docs/ddflow/mcp-soft-upgrade.md): reconnect is a fallback tier only, kept as a task; drop it if the Qwen probe shows no stdio-exit notice.

Present R-soft-* and the recommendation; settle: (1) A+D over B/C-only, (2) worker transport: stdio pipes to a child (default, portable incl. Windows) vs unix socket, (3) the soft/hard definition in the phase body, (4) schema grace: worker accepts the previous schema's arguments for one version, (5) what happens for clients that ignore list_changed (hard, tell the user). Record with ddflow decision add --globs ddflow/mcpshim/**,ddflow/surfaces/mcp*.py. Do not start SU-shim before this is decided.

Item (5) revised by the client matrix: clients that ignore list_changed are not simply hard. Decide: facade mode (ddflow_search/ddflow_call, MTD-search-call) as the way to make upgrades soft for them, the per-call restart notice as the fallback, and the rule 'soft iff digest unchanged OR client honours OR facade on'. See docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md.

Operator questions 2026-10-21 (recorded verbatim in the session log) answered in docs/ddflow/research/mcp-client-matrix.md Part 2. Decide additionally: (6) identify by table + listen opt-in + observation (SU-observe-client-capability), no handshake probe; (7) adopt the 5-rung soft/hard rule in SU-upgrade-integration, in particular rung 3 'soft with features pending' (an additive change is soft for every client) and the operator's split 'hard only when no list_changed AND the pre-existing facade changed incompatibly'; (8) reconnect is a fallback tier only (SU-reconnect-fallback): no client lets a server request a reconnect, exit-and-respawn drops the in-flight call and most clients keep the stale list (R-soft-cc-stdio-respawn, R-soft-reconnect-source-matrix).

DECIDED 2026-10-21: items (1)-(8) settled as recommended; see docs/ddflow/mcp-soft-upgrade.md.

data.summary: The Bash hook [hooks].forbidden_commands matches any '--force', so an operator-authorised 'ddflow complete <id> --force --reason ...' (stale docs-only research items RM-client-exec-research etc.) is refused with no operator-approval path except editing config; the hook should allow 'complete --force' when --reason is given, or name how a person approves it per call.

decision add refuses as 'possible duplicate' of the very task it was recorded for (--item SU-decision, duplicate-of SU-decision / SU-observe-client-capability); records of kind decision should be compared only against decisions (or at least not the --item task), else every decision made by a *-decide task needs --new.
